title: variable-length interleaver and temporal compression reporter for mixed-sequence benchmarks
author: Sofia Patel
commits: a1f3c2d: introduce VarLenInterleaver workload runner with sequence gating and stochastic padding
b2d4e8f: add TemporalCompressionReporter and output serialization to ndjson
c3e7f90: wire runner->reporter through bench pipeline and config knobs
d4f1a22: add unit tests and small integration harness for short/long mixes
e5b9c34: fix edge cases around empty prefix caching and add docs snippet
description:
Context: We need a representative workload that exercises variable-length prompts interleaved in the same session to measure the practical batching and KV-cache benefits for real product traffic. The existing seq-mix runners synthesize length distributions but do not model interleaving where short queries are frequently followed by long completions and where prefix redundancy can be exploited. This PR adds a new VarLenInterleaver runner that synthesizes interleaved sequences with configurable correlation, hotspot keys, and temporal locality. It also introduces a TemporalCompressionReporter that analyzes a run and computes compression-like metrics (prefix redundancy ratio, average retained KV size, effective token compression factor) to estimate how much batching and prefix/KV cache would reduce token work.

Motivation: give the perf team and model-onboarding engineers a quantitative signal for when prefix caching and short-short coalescing yield wins and to create a consistent baseline for regression testing.

Summary of changes: 1) New runner: VarLenInterleaver - generates sessions with alternating short and long sequences, supports seedable hotspots, correlation coefficient between sequence lengths, and an optional priming phase to emulate warmed KV caches. 2) New reporter: TemporalCompressionReporter - post-processes traces and produces per-epoch metrics including compression_ratio, p50/p95 retained_kv_size, redundant_token_fraction, and a summary suggestion for batching/window parameters. 3) Pipeline integration: mix_runner_pipeline.yaml wires the new runner and reporter into nightly bench pipelines with toggles for ramp profiles and sample weighting. 4) Tests and docs: unit tests for edge cases, small integration harness, and docs recipe for running the mixed-length benchmark locally and in CI.

Checklist: - [x] design doc discussion on Linear ENG-2142; - [x] unit and integration tests added; - [x] CI passes on Linux python3.11 runner; - [x] perf sanity numbers collected; - [x] docs recipe updated.

Performance notes: On a local canary run against a 32k-context LLM emulation we observed an empirical reduction in effective per-token compute of 8-12% when enabling prefix reuse heuristics, with p95 latency for mixed sessions decreasing ~9% under the recommended window settings. These numbers are noisy and depend on kernel selection and model sequence geometry; the reporter outputs epoch-by-epoch breakdowns to help triage.

Commits summary: a1f3c2d adds the core runner with a deterministic generator; b2d4e8f implements the reporter and ndjson output; c3e7f90 integrates components into the pipeline; d4f1a22 adds tests; e5b9c34 fixes an off-by-one in kv retention heuristics.

Changed areas (high level): varlen_interleaver.py contains the runner algorithm and configuration parsing; temporal_compression_reporter.py implements the compression metrics and console/ndjson sinks; pipeline yaml shows how to enable the runner in nightly jobs; seq_utils.py adds small helpers for rolling window similarity tests; tests exercise deterministic seeds and corner cases such as no-hotspot and single-sequence sessions.

Review conversation: Reviewer Diego Ramirez: "Nice approach, the compression metrics look useful. Can we add a metric for 'expected batch window' that suggests a batching window size?" Author reply (Sofia): "Added a simple heuristic in the reporter to emit a suggested_window_ms based on observed inter-arrival quantiles; documented it in the recipe." Reviewer Maya Nguyen: "Tests are good but I saw a flaky assertion in test_temporal_compression when run under high load. Can we make the test tolerant to sampling variance?" Author: "Adjusted test to use statistical tolerances and seed the RNG to ensure determinism in CI. Also added a retry wrapper for the flaky integration step." Reviewer Tom Becker: "Can the runner be extended to generate cross-session shared prefixes? That would help estimate cache priming across tenant migrations." Author: "That's orthogonal but straightforward; added a note in the code and an open follow-up ENG-2219 to track cross-session prefix sharing."

Approval: Diego approved after CR fixes; Maya approved after test tolerance fix; Tom approved with follow-up noted.

CI: Linux py3.11 bench pipeline succeeded; a flaky integration case initially failed on a heisenbug and was re-run and passed.

Merge: squash merge into main; merge commit message references ENG-2142 and SUP-1187.

Backwards compatibility: no changes to existing runner interfaces; new modules are additive and gated behind pipeline config.

Release notes: "Add VarLenInterleaver workload runner and TemporalCompressionReporter. New metrics help quantify prefix redundancy and recommend batching/window parameters for mixed-length session workloads."

How to run locally: see benchmark-lab/docs/bench-recipes.md recipe "varlen-interleaver" which documents config knobs: hotspot_ratio, correlation_coeff, priming_fraction, sample_weight.

Follow-ups: track cross-session prefix sharing support (ENG-2219); consider adding a lightweight Rust port of the reporter for tighter integration with the telemetry pipeline.

Merge method: squash. Merge sha: "f6d3b9a".
